name: Carrier name, MCC and MNC
plain: Android reads carrier and country codes with no prompt; iOS now returns placeholders.
meaning: Reveals the person's carrier, home country and roaming. Apple deprecated CTCarrier in iOS 16 and returns static values.

ios.api_surface: Returns placeholder values (MCC and MNC 65535) with no prompt

limits.headline: Can see your carrier name and country code on Android, not iPhone
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app checks your network
can: Get your carrier name on Android
Find your mobile country and network codes (MCC and MNC)
Guess your country from the codes
cannot: Get real carrier codes on iPhone; it returns placeholders
See your phone number or SIM serial
limits.differs: Android shows carrier name and codes with no prompt. iPhone now returns placeholder values (65535).

story.what_it_is: An app can see which mobile carrier you use and which country it is from.
story.for_you: You do not see it. Apps may show local offers or know that you are roaming. It tells them where your SIM comes from, even if you deny location.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for regional features, fraud checks and to see if a user is abroad. Ad systems also use carrier and country codes to target. Apple now gives apps fixed placeholder values.

use_cases.example: A bank app sees a foreign carrier and asks extra questions before a transfer.
A travel app shows roaming tips and local eSIM offers when it sees you are abroad.
A ride app picks the local payment methods that match your carrier's country.
An ad network sells a campaign aimed at one carrier's subscribers.
A game opens a regional store and price list from the country your SIM comes from.
A fraud system compares the SIM country with the sign up country to catch fakes.

story.android_note: Android apps can read carrier name, country code and network codes with no prompt.
story.ios_note: iPhone apps now get static placeholders because Apple deprecated the carrier API in iOS 16.
